summary: The translation is complete and mostly faithful, but it has real errors against the Hebrew: ימים rendered 'years', 'bathes at their expense' for the Aramaic 'relies on them', 'everlasting ground' for קרקע עולם, 'a king of kings' for 'a king from among the kings', 'had grown fat' for 'whom he counted', 'slander' for 'spoke rebellion', 'since' and 'his generation' added, and 'enlightened' against the ruling. Many sentences start in lower case after a Hebrew full stop or carry a full stop the Hebrew lacks; these are fixed, with a main clause supplied where the Hebrew fragment has none. Verses were missing from the apparatus (Joel 2:13 was given as Exod 34:6), the 'quick to anger' notes were missing, and the partzuf names lacked their literal sense. The three unresolved abbreviations: R. A. stays by the ruling, with a note that the story is Rabbi Eliezer's; ב״ע is read 'in Aramaic' with alternatives; הינ״ץ stays unexpanded with a conjecture (the Imam). Four questions are raised for the owner.

patches.value: And at the turn of the third year the war broke out against the good studies and the pleasant arrangements, as we are commanded by our Rabbis of blessed memory. The opponents spread an evil slander, saying that through this the children have gone out, God forbid, into bad ways, and many of the fools believed their lies and took their children out of the school. Also the foolish boys who had gone out of the school are hostile toward their teachers, because in their humble opinion they are heretics and stand outside the community. But those of understanding among them know and recognise that a lie is in the right hand of those who spread this evil slander, and they were greatly distressed that their fathers had taken them out of school in their folly! And when they had led many astray, the hand of the benighted grew strong and by false informing they informed against the teachers before the government, that they wished to incite the inhabitants of the land to rebel. And they informed that they were writers of libel against the government, to the government of England, to shelter in its shadow, and also to H.N.Ts. And because of this informing the teachers were led to prison, and also expelled from the school. And they brought in their place another teacher, who knew neither Hebrew thoroughly nor Arabic as it should be. And he had no duty to teach them except the weekly portion, with the Targum of Onkelos and the Targum of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic. And he was to teach them the Haftarah with the Targum of Jonathan in Aramaic, with no understanding at all, like the other teachers! And after some days the school closed entirely! All this came upon us because we did not object, for the honour of our Creator, when we were hearing from those who study the Zohar and other Kabbalists, things that are forbidden to hear, and we were silent before them as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "R. A. was seized for heresy, etc.; perhaps a word of heresy, etc." and there was fulfilled in us the saying of our Rabbis of blessed memory: "Whoever concedes to them falls into their hands; whoever relies on them, what is his is theirs." Thus far! Therefore we abandoned our way of studying the languages, Hebrew and Arabic, in their grammar, against our will, because of the wrath of the oppressor, through false informing, and we turned to the path of holiness, to the honour of our Father who is in heaven, in the nullification of the opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the author of the Zohar, who gathered into his hands the opinions of ancient philosophy, the worshippers of idols, images and hidden powers, which they had invented from their own heart. And the author of the Zohar seized their opinions, and thought to bring them into the faith of our holy Torah, and falsely called his name by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, and said that the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called by him Atika Kadisha, was revealed to him and revealed to him hidden mysteries. And he hung his prophecy and his ideas on Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him. And he made his composition, the Zohar, and said that the higher ones agreed to his composition, because this philosopher saw that the Mishnah, the two Talmuds and the true midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory stood against him in the belief in His oneness, may He be blessed, therefore he thought to disqualify them, and he despised and mocked them and all who occupy themselves with them, and he called them by names of contempt and abasement, as the reader will see within! And he promised that Israel would not merit redemption until they turned from their way of occupying themselves with the Mishnah and the Talmud. Let them occupy themselves only with his new Torah, full of idols of images and faces of monstrous form, and various couplings. And by cunning and deceit they buried it in a chest in the ground, so that it would grow old and begin to rot; after some time they published it and brought it out through a king from among the kings of the idolaters (as Rabbi Chida wrote in his book Shem ha-Gedolim, in the section on books), as if it were an ancient composition of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna. And many of our later rabbis were drawn after the aforementioned philosopher with eyes shut, for he took them with the smoothness of his lips and his trimmings, and they did not give heed to his lies! Heaven forbid that any Jew should believe that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna or another of our Rabbis of blessed memory believed in such beliefs to exchange and replace the LORD our God, who made known His ways to Moses and His deeds to the children of Israel, for "He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness," etc. for a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), and to conjoin and associate with Him five partzufim whose existence has not been established even by proof (Rabbi Ovadiah Sforno, Deuteronomy 13:3; and there 29:25; and see there 28:14) and to call them by the name of the LORD our God, and the LORD, the God of truth, whose existence has been established by many proofs, strong as a cast mirror, as Rabbi Saadia Gaon wrote in Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rabbi, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and the Rambam in Moreh Nevukhim and in the Yad, let us abandon Him and leave Him, and say that He has no name and no appellation, and let us worship the partzufim and the forms which, according to his words, were created and descended from Him! And we have already expounded at length within, with clear proofs from our Rabbis of blessed memory, on the nullification of these strange opinions of the philosopher, the false prophet, the aforementioned! For it is the aim of our holy Torah to distance us from belief in idols, whether corporeal or spiritual. And its aim is to know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him. And He has neither father nor brother nor son (Rabbah, parashat Yitro), and did not receive His kingship from another and is not destined to hand it on to another, as our Rabbis of blessed memory explained (Rabbah, Bamidbar; Shir ha-Shirim, parashah 1; Yerushalmi, Sanhedrin, chapter Dinei Mamonot) on the verse "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God," and on what Nebuchadnezzar said: "and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods!" And I have seen Rabbi Menachem di Lonzano, in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, who opened his mouth wide to speak error about the holy pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, concerning his saying, in the name of the philosopher, that one could not worship the Cause of causes, except the prophet of the generation by his nature, or the outstanding philosopher in what he acquired from wisdom; but others worship other than Him, because they do not understand: the result is only composite! And at these words of the pietist he was angered and thought that here was ground for complaint against him, and found a pretext to mislead the listeners and alarm them by saying: "Is it so that such-and-such and such-and-such of our later famous sages worship other than Him?" And he counted them, in his language, one by one by name. And he did not take to heart that many of the sages whom he counted went along with eyes shut and believed the words of the author of the Zohar who called himself by the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, in order to attach his false prophecies to the name of the Tanna, and spoke rebellion against the LORD our God, who was revealed to him in his study house as Atika Kadisha, and revealed to him hidden secrets and hidden powers (Zohar, Bereshit 22), for the Creator is the idol called Abba, who used to command his consort, the she-idol Imma, and she does all that he says to her, except for the creation of the first man: it was she, Imma, who said and made the first man, not with the will of Abba! And in Parashat Vayera, folio 112, and likewise in Parashat Balak, folio 191, he ascribes our worship and our prayers to a strange god, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), who did not make the heavens and the earth. And he calls these idols by the name of the LORD our God. And about Ze'ir Anpin, Jeremiah the prophet, peace be upon him, proclaimed "Thus shall you say to them: the gods that did not make the heavens and the earth shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens." For it is clear in many places in the Zohar that he is created, not creator (see Zohar, Bereshit 22; and Yosher Levav, folio 3b). And yet he says to worship him, and to bless him, and to accept him as God, and to fear his consort! And many of our later rabbis, whom he mentioned in the book Derekh ha-Chayyim, in his amazement at the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, went along with eyes shut and were drawn after him and believed his belief and accepted upon themselves the idol, quick to anger (Ze'ir Anpin), as God! And all this came upon them because they did not contemplate the wisdom of the Creator of all, which is to investigate and examine the works of Creation as explained in the words of the Rabbi, the author of Moreh Nevukhim, and in the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and our master Saadia Gaon and Rabbi Yehudah Halevi in the Kuzari, as the prophet, peace be upon him, said: "They do not regard the deed of the LORD." For they thought their words were Greek wisdom, and they kept far from it, as far as a bow-shot, and they also did not take to heart the true words of our forefathers of blessed memory in the midrashim that Abraham our father did not recognise his Creator except by contemplating the work of the LORD, and investigated and expounded them and brought proofs from them until he attained the truth; then the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed to him and said to him: "You love righteousness and hate wickedness," etc. A parable: to one walking on the road who saw a castle, etc. (Midrash ha-Gadol, at the beginning of Parashat Lekh Lekha). And perforce we acknowledge the truth that the words of the pietist, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, clearly say that one cannot worship the God of truth except, etc. but others worship other than Him, as the prophet said: "For many days Israel was without a true God," and as our eyes see and our ears hear, to the point that a man can say to his fellow! "Your people is my people, and your God is not my God!" And to the God of truth let us pour out our prayer, to guide us on paths of uprightness, and to deliver us from every strange belief. Amen, may it be His will.
patches.reason: Faults against the Hebrew and the decisions: 'in the third year' drops תקופת ('at the turn of'); 'would go out' for the perfect יצאו, and 'education' for תרבות רעה ('bad ways', the idiom for going wrong); המשכילים is 'those of understanding' (the ruling: 'the enlightened' only where the paragraph speaks of the Haskalah); התעו is Hif'il, 'they led many astray'; להמריד is 'to incite to rebel'; 'על בריה' (printed) for על בוריה, so the teacher did not know Hebrew thoroughly, not 'no Hebrew at all'; ימים is 'days', not 'years' (לימים מספר, אחר ימים); דמתרחץ is Aramaic 'relies on' (רחץ, to trust), not 'bathes at their expense'; קרקע עולם is 'the ground', not 'everlasting ground'; להתיישן ויתחיל is purpose ('so that it would grow old and begin to rot'); מלך ממלכי is 'a king from among the kings'; the parentheses round 'as Rabbi Chida wrote' were dropped; 'full of idols of images, faces' drops the ו between תמונות and פרצופים (the ruling gives 'idols of images and faces of monstrous form'); לצרף is 'conjoin' (the ruling for צירוף of God); 'the Guide for the Perplexed' for במורה נבוכים (titles are transliterated); 'since He is not destined' adds a connective (ואינו עתיד); 'that Rabbi Menchem' adds 'that' (and the name is Menachem); הדור is 'the generation', not 'his generation', and המובהק is definite; 'שמנה' is 'whom he counted', not 'had grown fat' (cf. 1:4.844-847); 'ודבר סרה' is 'spoke rebellion' (Deut 13:6), not 'slander'; ועשתה את אדם הראשון is 'made the first man' (the object was dropped); 'He is created' puts a capital on Ze'ir Anpin where the ruling forbids editorialising by case, and the fixed form is 'created, not creator'; בתמיהתו is 'in his amazement' (Lonzano's), not 'in their'; 'took offence' for התקצף ('was angered'); וכי is 'is it so that'; 'and our master Rabbi Saadia' adds 'Rabbi'; 'must' is added to ועל כרחנו נודה. Punctuation: a full stop and lower-case start where the Hebrew has none ('dinei mamonot). on the verse'; '(Zohar, Bereshit 22). for the Creator'; 'no God." and on what'; '..., And we turned'), lower-case 'and'/'for' after a Hebrew full stop (ושהם, והפטרה, ולדעת, ואין לו, ולא שם, שהרי, כי חשבו, כי הוא), and an invented full stop before the quoted-verse clause. The sentences that open after a full stop with no main clause take one from the sentence before, as the ruling for שכל/שהוא provides (see the question).

patches.reason: The English of the segment changed; the phrases are carried over with the same token spans, and the phrases that held the changed punctuation (the period after the parenthesis, the period inside the Isa 44:6 quotation, the split at the Chida parenthesis) are re-cut.
תקופה is 'turn, season'; the English dropped it.
Passive participle; 'as we are commanded'.
יצאו is perfect, not 'would go out'.
תרבות is 'culture, upbringing', not 'education'.

patches.value: 'יצא לתרבות רעה' (went out to bad ways) is the idiom for going wrong; the English is 'bad ways'.
patches.reason: A learner needs the idiom.
Ruling: משכילים is 'the educated' / 'enlightenment' only where the paragraph speaks of the Haskalah; otherwise 'those of understanding'.
התעו is Hif'il (transitive).

patches.value: Hif'il perfect, 'they led astray', with רבים as its object.
patches.reason: Learner note.
'Obscurantists' names a later party; the Hebrew says 'those of darkness'.
Hif'il of מרד; 'to incite' drops the rebellion.

patches.value: ושהם opens after a full stop with no main clause of its own; the English supplies 'they informed' from הלשינו (1:4.83), as the ruling for ש-clauses provides.
patches.reason: Ruling: 'A sentence opening שכל / שהוא after a full stop: keep the full stop and supply a main clause, with a token note on the ש.'
על with כותבי פלסתר is 'against' (a libel against the government), not 'about'.
Part of the idiom על בוריה (see 1:4.130).

patches.value: 'על בריה' as printed; the likelier word is על בוריה, 'thoroughly'. No idiom 'al briyah' meaning 'at all' is known; the parallel 'כתקנה' (as it should be) also asks for a manner word.
patches.reason: The earlier note invents an idiom. Ruling: a word close to a likelier one is translated by the context, with the printed word in a token note and the apparatus.
בוריה, 'its clarity, fullness' (printed בריה).

patches.value: Printed בריה ('creature'); read as בוריה. 'לא ידע עברית על בוריה' means he did not know Hebrew thoroughly.
והפטרה opens after a full stop with no main clause of its own; it continues 'ואין עליו ללמדם רק' (1:4.134-137), and the English supplies 'he was to teach them'. See the question.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent on a noun fragment after a Hebrew full stop (the ruling covers ש-clauses and אם...או). Proposed ruling: supply a main clause from the sentence before when the fragment continues its verb; join with a comma only when it continues a list (as at 1:4.896).
No article; parallel to 'in Arabic' (1:4.145).

patches.value: ב״ע is read 'in Aramaic' (בארמית): the Haftarah is taught with the Aramaic Targum alone, with no Arabic beside it, so the pupils 'understand nothing'. Other readings: בעל פה ('by heart') and בערבי ('in Arabic'); see readings.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent on ב״ע. Proposed ruling: 'in Aramaic' by the contrast with בערבי at 1:4.145 and with 'באין הבין כלום', alternatives in readings; not certain.
ימים is 'days', not 'years'.
ימים מספר (Num 9:20) is 'a few days'.
Learner note.

patches.value: דר״א: ד (that) + ר״א. The story of the Rabbi seized for minut (heresy) is told of Rabbi Eliezer; the paragraph names no Rabbi, so the English keeps 'R. A.' as the ruling for ר״א requires ('Rabbi Eleazar' only where the paragraph names him).
patches.reason: The ruling asks for a note saying who is meant; the old note ('a Talmudic Rabbi') says nothing.
Aramaic Itpa'al of רחץ, 'to trust, rely' (Dan 3:28 רחצו עלוהי), not 'bathe'.

patches.value: Aramaic: דמתרחץ (that trusts / relies), Itpa'al of רחץ.
patches.reason: Learner note.
עליהון is 'on them'; 'at their expense' has no basis.
דיליה ('that which is his').

patches.value: Atika Kadisha (Zohar Aramaic): 'Holy Ancient One', a partzuf; transliterated by the ruling.
patches.reason: Ruling: names of the partzufim carry the literal sense in a note at the first occurrence in a unit.

patches.value: ופרצופים: here the generic 'faces' (paired with תמונות), with a play on the partzufim of the Kabbalists.
patches.reason: Ruling: the generic sense is 'face'; where the author plays on both senses, add a note.
קרקע עולם is the ground itself.
'עולם' is not 'everlasting' in the idiom קרקע עולם.

patches.value: קרקע עולם: the ground itself (not 'everlasting ground').
patches.reason: Learner note.
אחר ימים is 'after some time', with no 'many'.
מלך ממלכי is 'a king from among the kings of', not 'a king of kings'.

patches.value: גיזומיו: 'his cuttings, trimmings'; possibly from the Aramaic גוזמא, 'exaggeration'. See the question.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent. 'Trimmings' is an odd English word for what the Hebrew pairs with 'smoothness of his lips'. Proposed ruling: 'his exaggerations'.

patches.value: 'Slow to anger': the author's verse is Joel 2:13 (cf. Exod 34:6); the pair of 'quick to anger' below.
patches.reason: The words 'כי חנון ורחום הוא ארך אפים ורב חסד' are Joel 2:13, not Exod 34:6.
Titles are transliterated (decisions): Moreh Nevukhim.
Titles are transliterated (decisions).
ואינו: 'and', not 'since'; the English added a connective.
'that' is not in the Hebrew (the ל is 'regarding / of').
Project scheme: ח = ch, with the vowel; 'Menchem' drops one.
נביא הדור is definite.
הדור has no possessive ('his generation').
הפילסוף המובהק is definite.
התקצף is 'was angry'.
The context ('one by one by name', 1:4.676-680; 'whom he mentioned', 1:4.847) requires שֶׁמָּנָה; the pointing שַמָנָה would be 'grew fat'.

patches.value: Printed שַמָנָה (would be 'grew fat', Deut 32:15); read שֶׁמָּנָה 'whom he counted' by the context; the alternative is in readings and the apparatus.
patches.reason: Ruling: a word that does not fit its context but is close to a likelier one is translated by the context, with both in a token note and apparatus.
דבר סרה (Deut 13:6) is 'spoke rebellion'; 'slander' is not the sense.

patches.value: 'ודבר סרה על ה'': Deut 13:6, the verse on the false prophet; cf. Isa 59:13.
patches.reason: The verse should be recognised: the author applies the law of the false prophet.

patches.value: Abba: Aramaic 'Father'; a partzuf. Transliterated by the ruling.
patches.reason: Ruling: names of the partzufim carry the literal sense in a note at the first occurrence.

patches.value: Imma: Aramaic 'Mother'; a partzuf. Transliterated by the ruling.
patches.reason: Ruling: as for Abba.

patches.value: Calque of Ze'ir Anpin (Aramaic 'small face'), set against 'slow to anger' (Exod 34:6). Prov 14:17.
patches.reason: Ruling for קצר אפים: 'Add a note each time'.
Ruling: no editorialising by case; Ze'ir Anpin is 'he' in the author's charge.
The suffix of בתמיהתו is third masculine singular (Lonzano's), not 'their'.

patches.value: Calque of Ze'ir Anpin (Aramaic 'small face'), set against 'slow to anger' (Exod 34:6). Prov 14:17.
patches.reason: Ruling for קצר אפים: 'Add a note each time'.

patches.value: הינ״ץ: left unexpanded in the English. Conjecture: ה + ינ״ץ, 'ינצרהו צורו' ('may his Rock protect him'), an honorific that follows a ruler's name; in 8:11 the informers write to 'the Imam' (האימאם יר״ה), so 'the Imam, may his Rock protect him' is likely meant. Not certain.
patches.reason: Decisions cover only יר״ה for the Imam. Proposed ruling: leave 'H.N.Ts.' in the English with this note, unless the owner accepts 'the Imam, may his Rock protect him', which would identify a person the ruling says to leave unidentified.

value: Voice: 1:4 is in the author's own voice; 'we' (עלינו, עזבנו, נודה) is the author and the circle of the Yemenite teachers. The long periods are divided into English sentences, and no clause is dropped.

Aramaic quotations: 1:4.198-206 (דמודי להון) is Bavli Aramaic; 1:4.274-275 (עתיקא קדישא) and 1:4.278 (רזין טמירין) are Zohar Aramaic; 1:4.591-600 is Biblical Aramaic (Dan 3:25) and 1:4.800-815 is Biblical Aramaic (Jer 10:11).

Allusions with no quotation formula are translated from the verse and take no marks: 'שקר בימין' (1:4.61-62, Isa 44:20), 'בחלק שפתיו' (1:4.396-397, Prov 7:21), and 'ולדעת כי ה' הוא האלהים אין עוד מלבדו' (1:4.540-547, Deut 4:35). The other verses behind the author's phrases are listed in the apparatus.

1:4.667 'וכי' opens a rhetorical question, kept as a question. 1:4.688 'שַמָנָה' as pointed would be 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15), but the context requires 'שֶׁמָּנָה', 'whom he counted': he counted the sages 'one by one by name' (1:4.676-680), and 1:4.844-847 says the same again ('whom he mentioned'). The English follows the context.

1:4.76 התעו is Hif'il, 'they led astray' (transitive, with רבים as object). 1:4.90 להמריד is Hif'il of מרד, 'to make rebel'. 1:4.198-206 is Aramaic: דמתרחץ is Itpa'al of רחץ 'to trust, to rely' (cf. Dan 3:28 רחצו עלוהי), not 'to bathe'.

Sentences that open after a Hebrew full stop with no main clause of their own: 1:4.94 ושהם, 1:4.146 והפטרה, 1:4.540 ולדעת. The English keeps the full stop and supplies a main clause from the sentence before (token notes); 1:4.896 ורבינו is a continuation of a list and is joined to the sentence before it.
patches.reason: The note on 1:4.688 followed the printed pointing; the context requires 'whom he counted'. Notes added on the Hif'il forms, the Aramaic רחץ, and the sentences that open after a full stop.

value: Base text: Wikisource transcription. Q2 additions are translated as base text and are not yet collated with the 1931 scan.
1:4.62 'a lie in the right hand' alludes to Isa 44:20.
1:4.396 'the smoothness of his lips' alludes to Prov 7:21.

1:4.429-437 'He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness' is Joel 2:13 (cf. Exod 34:6, Jonah 4:2), cut short by the author with 'etc.'; the author's 'quick to anger' (1:4.440-441, 1:4.775-776, 1:4.866-867) is set against it.
1:4.478-480 'strong as a cast mirror' is Job 37:18 (Hebrew 'strong like a cast mirror').
1:4.454-465 references as the author gives them: Sforno on Deut 13:3, 29:25, 28:14.
1:4.584-590 Isa 44:6: 'I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God'.
1:4.591-600 Dan 3:25 (Biblical Aramaic).
1:4.800-815 Jer 10:11 (Biblical Aramaic); 'gods' renders Aramaic elahaya.
1:4.910 Isa 5:12, quoted by the author.
1:4.1001-1006 2 Chr 15:3, quoted by the author as 'the prophet'.
1:4.1017-1021 Ruth 1:16 with the negation the author gives ('your God is not my God'); the English follows his wording.
1:4.107 'הינ״ץ' is not expanded in the English; the expansion is not certain. A conjecture is in the token note (see the question).

1:4.150 'ב״ע' is read 'in Aramaic' (the Targum to the Haftarah, set against 'בערבי' for the Torah portion at 1:4.145, so that the pupils understand nothing); the other expansions, 'בעל פה' ('by heart') and 'בערבי' ('in Arabic'), are in readings. None is certain.
1:4.186 'ר״א' (in 'דר״א') is the author's abbreviation, left as 'R. A.' by the ruling, since the paragraph names no Rabbi; the token note says who is meant.
1:4.1034 'אכי״ר' expanded as 'may it be His will' (אמן כן יהי רצון).
1:4.14-17 and 1:4.63-65 'spread an evil slander' / 'those who spread this evil slander' echo Num 14:37 (מוציאי דבה רעה).
1:4.129-130 'על בריה' as printed ('on a creature'); the likelier word is 'על בוריה' ('thoroughly'), which the English follows.
1:4.162-164 'All this came upon us' is Ps 44:18.
1:4.202-203 'דמתרחץ עליהון' is read 'whoever relies on them' (Aramaic רחץ, 'to trust'; cf. Dan 3:28).
1:4.218-219 'the wrath of the oppressor' is Isa 51:13 (חמת המציק).
1:4.226-227 'the path of holiness' is Isa 35:8 (דרך הקדש).
1:4.239-240 'gathered into his hands' alludes to Prov 30:4 (אסף ... בחפניו).
1:4.250-251 'invented from their own heart' alludes to 1 Kgs 12:33 and Neh 6:8 (בדא / בודא מלבו).
1:4.357-358 'בקרקע עולם' is the idiom for the ground itself, not 'everlasting ground'.
1:4.423-428 'who made known His ways to Moses and His deeds to the children of Israel' is Ps 103:7.
1:4.471-473 'the LORD, the God of truth' is Jer 10:10 (ה' אלהים אמת).
1:4.611-612 'to speak error' is Isa 32:6 (ולדבר אל ה' תועה).
1:4.688 'שַמָנָה' as printed would be 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15); the likelier word is 'שֶׁמָּנָה' ('whom he counted'), which the English follows (see readings).
1:4.710-711 'ודבר סרה על ה'' ('spoke rebellion against the LORD') is Deut 13:6 (cf. Isa 59:13).
1:4.918-920 'as far as a bow-shot' is Gen 21:16 (כמטחוי קשת).
1:4.956-959 'You love righteousness and hate wickedness' is Ps 45:8.
1:4.985-986 'ברור מללו' ('clearly say') echoes Job 33:3.
1:4.1025-1026 'let us pour out our prayer' echoes Ps 142:3.
patches.reason: The verse behind 'He is gracious and compassionate...' is Joel 2:13, not Exod 34:6. Verses missing (the ruling asks for each verse the reviewer can verify): Num 14:37, Ps 44:18, Isa 51:13, Isa 35:8, Prov 30:4, 1 Kgs 12:33 / Neh 6:8, Ps 103:7, Jer 10:10, Isa 32:6, Deut 13:6, Gen 21:16, Ps 45:8, Job 33:3, Ps 142:3. The variants (על בריה, שַמָנָה, ב״ע, ר״א, הינ״ץ) are recorded as the ruling asks.

value.note: ב״ע read as בעל פה: the Targum recited by rote, which would suit 'with no understanding at all'.

value.english: in Arabic
value.note: ב״ע read as בערבי, the abbreviation of the 'in Arabic' of 1:4.145.

value.english: and his exaggerations
value.note: גיזומיו may come from the Aramaic גוזמא, 'exaggeration'; the English keeps 'trimmings' (cuttings) pending the owner's ruling.

value.english: had grown fat
value.note: The pointing שַמָנָה reads as 'grew fat' (Deut 32:15); the context requires 'whom he counted'.

patches.reason: Missing readings: the other expansions of ב״ע, 'exaggerations' for גיזומיו, and the pointed שַמָנָה.

value: Chida is Rabbi Chayyim Yosef David Azulai; his Shem ha-Gedolim is a bibliographical dictionary of Jewish authors and books, which the author cites here.
Ze'ir Anpin, Abba, Imma and Atika Kadisha are the partzufim of the Zohar's divine structure. The author calls them idols in his own charge, and the English gives his words as he writes them.

Saadia Gaon's Arabic translation of the Torah is taught in Yemenite communities beside the Aramaic Targum Onkelos; Targum Jonathan is the Aramaic Targum to the Prophets, from which the Haftarah is read.
patches.reason: A reader needs the Yemenite custom behind 'the Targum of Onkelos and the Targum of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic'.
